source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #266 (#209, per-function JIT trap-site tables). The PR records, for every native trap site a baseline emitter produces, the decoded-stream pc index of the emitting instruction in a per-function table (Vec<u32>), packs the 1-based site id into the trap exit value (code | site << 8; site 0 keeps the previous bare-code encoding for stub-raised traps), resolves the site against the trapping function's own table at the innermost JIT entry boundary, and charges the table bytes to the code-cache budget. Landing it required merging current main (PR #265, #197's EmitEnv generalisation) into the branch: the three backend files and backend.rs conflicted, and were resolved onto #197's structure — the per-arch emitters stay generic over EmitEnv and their Emission result gains the trap-site table, Emitter::finish() returns the code plus the table, and return_trap keeps recording sites and packing the exit value in both modes. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main (a4177b4) alone (workflow_dispatch run 45115401237, gate success): it reproduces the previous baseline exactly on all 28 gated series, so every delta is this PR’s own. The growth is confined to the core-jit configuration, the only one that links the JIT backends into the minimal embedder (release stripped file +2,384 B / stripped .text +2,128 B; release-size stripped file +880 B / stripped .text +816 B), plus a +16 B code-layout shift in the release-size component configuration (stripped file and stripped .text), attributable to the ExecuteContext field the PR appends in the shared runtime — the only part of the change linked into non-JIT configurations; the other 25 gated series are byte-identical. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series (14 profile/configuration rows x stripped file and stripped .text, n=3; the raw file and .text sizes were also identical across the three runs), so each threshold equals its observed baseline exactly (baseline + 0). Any further growth requires an intentional re-baseline; see docs/benchmarks/footprint.md, ‘Size regression gate (#164)’. The four core-aot series were added by the #200 change (aot-load feature split): they were measured with the same tool on the change branch at fleur-du-lapin (Linux x86_64, Xeon Gold 6140, Rust 1.96.0, --sizes-only, one run per profile; the existing series measured in the same runs matched this baseline within 312 B, the code-layout shift of the cfg refactor), and they gate the new configuration from its first CI run; the merge-time re-baseline on CI runners supersedes these values like every other row.
